surprises.head: A rough night for Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen
surprises.body: Luukkonen allowed 5 goals on 22 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

surprises.head: Columbus brought the hits
surprises.body: Columbus’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 163, against their usual 99 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: The Blue Jackets beat the Sabres
paras: Valeri Nichushkin made his Blue Jackets debut, after seven seasons with the Avalanche, and picked up an assist. Emil Andrae made his Blue Jackets debut, after three seasons with the Flyers, and picked up an assist. It was a busy first period. Mattias Samuelsson opened the scoring for the Sabres midway through the period, but Cole Sillinger tied it up for Columbus later in the period. Matthew Knies and Adam Fantilli scored 46 seconds apart late in the period to put the Blue Jackets up 3-1. Jack Quinn pulled the Sabres within one early in the second, and Zach Metsa and Mathieu Olivier dropped the gloves early in the period. Knies scored his second of the night midway through the period to make it 4-2 for the Jackets. Konsta Helenius pulled the Sabres within one later in the period, but that was as close as they got. Sean Monahan stretched the lead to 5-3 on the power play late in the third, and Olivier added an empty-net goal with just over two minutes left to make it 6-3. There were two three-point nights: Charlie Coyle with three assists, and Knies with two goals and an assist.
The Sabres had a little more of the play. The Blue Jackets had the finish. Jet Greaves made 23 saves for the Blue Jackets, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed five goals on 22 shots.

The Blue Jackets killed all five Sabres power plays. The Blue Jackets killed off a two-man advantage that lasted two minutes early in the second. The Sabres hit two posts and the crossbar, and the bounces never came. The Blue Jackets moved to 1-0-0, and the Sabres dropped to 0-1-0.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Blue Jackets won their home opener.
Matt Grzelcyk faces his old team, Chicago, on Saturday.
